heroData.title: Hire in Mexico (No Entity)
heroData.subtitle: REPSE Certified & USMCA Ready
heroData.description: The safest way to hire Mexican talent without a local subsidiary. We handle the complex 2021 Outsourcing Reform (REPSE) compliance, IMSS social security, and mandatory profit sharing (PTU) on your behalf.

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Drafting a 'Contrato Individual de Trabajo'. In Mexico, indefinite term contracts are the legal standard. Fixed-term or project-based contracts must have a specific, justifiable cause to avoid reclassification risks.

steps.title: IMSS & Infonavit Registration
steps.description: Employees must be registered with the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) on their very first day of work. The EOR partner handles the registration, ensuring the 'Salario Base de Cotización' (SBC) is calculated correctly including all statutory benefits.

steps.title: RFC & CURP Verification
steps.description: Collecting and verifying the employee's Tax ID (RFC) and Population Registry Code (CURP). This is critical for the 'Timbrado' (digital stamping) of payslips with the SAT tax authority.

steps.title: NOM-035 Medical/Psychosocial
steps.description: Establishing compliance with NOM-035 regulations, which include psychosocial risk assessments and potentially a medical check-up. The EOR ensures these records are kept in the employee's digital file (Expediente).

steps.title: Bilateral Handover
steps.description: Signing of the work equipment handover protocol and the 'Aviso de Privacidad' (Privacy Notice) as required by the Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data.

items.title: REPSE Certification Requirement
items.text: Since the 2021 Labor Reform, any EOR provider in Mexico MUST be registered with the STPS (Ministry of Labor) under the REPSE registry. Using a non-certified provider can lead to massive fines and the inability to deduct expenses for tax purposes.

items.title: Mandatory Profit Sharing (PTU)
items.text: Employees are legally entitled to 10% of the company's annual profits. When using an EOR, the EOR's profit in Mexico is subject to this, which is typically factored into the EOR fee structure to protect the client.

items.title: Aguinaldo (Year-end Bonus)
items.text: A mandatory 13th-month style bonus called Aguinaldo must be paid by December 20th. The legal minimum is 15 days of salary, though many international companies offer 20-30 days to remain competitive.

items.title: USMCA Visa Advantages
items.text: For US or Canadian citizens working via EOR in Mexico, the TN Visa (or FMM/Residency) process is streamlined under USMCA, making it easier to station management personnel locally while hiring a Mexican team.

items.title: Permanent Establishment (PE) Risk
items.text: If an EOR employee has the power to sign contracts or conclude sales on behalf of the foreign parent company, it might trigger a Permanent Establishment status, leading to corporate tax liabilities for the foreign entity in Mexico.

values: Varies based on the employer's risk category and salary level.

values: Mandatory employer contribution to the employee housing fund.

values: Depends on the state (CDMX is 3%, Nuevo Leon is 3%).

values: Typical overhead on top of the base gross salary.

faqs.question: Can I hire a contractor instead of using EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but there is significant 'misclassification risk'. If the contractor performs core business tasks, uses company equipment, or follows set hours, Mexican labor courts (which are very pro-employee) may deem them a de-facto employee, requiring full back-payment of benefits and taxes.

faqs.question: How long does the probation period last?
faqs.answer: The standard probation period is 30 days for general staff and up to 180 days for management or specialized personnel. Termination during this window is significantly easier and cheaper than post-probation.

faqs.question: Is insurance provided via the EOR?
faqs.answer: While IMSS provides public healthcare, most competitive EOR packages for white-collar talent include 'Gastos Médicos Mayores' (Private Major Medical Insurance) and Life Insurance as supplemental benefits.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle the annual tax return for the employee?
faqs.answer: No. Employees earning over 400,000 MXN per year or those with multiple income sources are responsible for their own annual filing (Declaración Anual) in April, though the EOR provides the necessary withholding certificates (Constancias).

faqs.question: What happens if there is a labor dispute?
faqs.answer: The EOR partner is the legal employer and is the first line of defense in a labor court. However, EOR contracts usually include indemnification clauses where the client covers costs if the termination was requested by the client.

items.title: Vales de Despensa (Food Vouchers)
items.text: Providing food vouchers (usually electronic cards) is a standard practice in Mexico. They are tax-deductible for the employer and tax-free for the employee up to certain limits, making them highly desirable.

items.title: Teletrabajo (Remote Work Law)
items.text: If an employee works >40% of their time remotely, the employer is legally required to provide ergonomic equipment and pay a prorated portion of internet and electricity costs.

items.title: Vacation Premium
items.text: Employees get a 'Prima Vacacional' (Vacation Premium) of at least 25% of their daily salary for each vacation day taken. This is a unique Mexican benefit aimed at helping employees enjoy their time off.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Processing salary inputs, overtime, bonuses, and commissions. Calculating Federal Tax (ISR) withholdings and both employer/employee shares of social security (IMSS).

steps.title: CFDI 4.0 Timbrado
steps.description: Generating the XML payroll receipt and sending it to an authorized PAC (Certification Provider) for the SAT digital stamp. This is the only legally valid proof of payment in Mexico.

steps.title: Interbank Disbursement (SPEI)
steps.description: Generating the bank payment files for the SPEI network. Payments are typically made bi-weekly (Quincenal) on the 15th and last day of the month.

steps.title: Social Security Filing (SUA/IDSE)
steps.description: Using the SUA (Self-Determination System) and IDSE (IMSS Data Exchange) platforms to report movements, incidences, and pay the monthly social security contributions.

steps.title: Monthly Tax Remittance
steps.description: Filing the ISR withholding return with the SAT and paying the corresponding state-level payroll tax (ISN) before the 17th of the following month.

items.title: CFDI 4.0 Strictness
items.text: Since 2023, CFDI 4.0 requires the exact tax address (Postal Code) and name of the employee as registered at the SAT. Any mismatch prevents the payslip from being stamped, making it impossible to deduct the payroll expense.

items.title: Bi-weekly vs Monthly
items.text: 90% of Mexican private sector employees are paid 'Quincenalmente' (every 15 days). Expecting a monthly cycle can lead to dissatisfaction and high turnover in local teams.

items.title: SBC Calculation Complexity
items.text: The Social Security base (SBC) is not just the base salary. It must include the 'Factor de Integración' which accounts for Aguinaldo and Vacation Premium portions on a daily basis. Errors here lead to significant IMSS audits.

items.title: Tax-Efficient Benefits
items.text: Judicious use of 'Previsión Social' (Social Welfare) benefits like savings funds (Fondo de Ahorro) and pantry vouchers can reduce the taxable base for both the employer and employee.

items.title: Annual PTU Cycle
items.text: Companies must distribute 10% of their prior year's taxable income to employees by May 30th (for corporations). This requires a specific payroll run with complex distribution formulas based on days worked and salary levels.

faqs.question: What is the 'Timbrado' deadline?
faqs.answer: The payslip must be digitally stamped (timbrado) either on the day of payment or within 3-11 business days after (depending on the number of employees). Delays make the expense non-deductible.

faqs.question: How do I calculate the ISN (State Tax)?
faqs.answer: It is calculated on the total gross payroll. The rate varies by state: CDMX (3%), State of Mexico (3%), Jalisco (3%), and Querétaro (3%). Some states have small exemptions for new companies.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable in Mexico?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most bonuses are subject to ISR. However, Aguinaldo is exempt up to 30 UMAs (approx 3,250 MXN) and Vacation Premium is exempt up to 15 UMAs (approx 1,625 MXN).

faqs.question: What happens if I underpay IMSS?
faqs.answer: The IMSS has aggressive automated audit tools. Underpayments result in fines of 40-100% of the omitted contribution, plus updates and surcharges (CPI adjustment).

faqs.question: Can I pay in US Dollars?
faqs.answer: No. While you can agree on a USD-linked amount in the contract, the actual payment and the CFDI receipt must be in Mexican Pesos (MXN) using the official exchange rate (FIX) from the day of payment.

items.text: Contributions to the AFORA system, ensuring the employee has a pension fund.

items.title: Social Security (IMSS)
items.text: Covers medical care, maternity, disability, and life insurance.

items.text: A 5% contribution enabling employees to access low-interest home loans.

steps.title: Base Salary Input
steps.description: Defining the 'Sueldo Diario' (Daily Salary) which serves as the base for all percentage-based calculations.

steps.title: Benefit Integration (Integrated Salary)
steps.description: Adding the 'Factor de Integración' (Aguinaldo + Vacation Premium) to arrive at the Salario Diario Integrado (SDI) used for IMSS.

steps.title: Withholding Application
steps.description: Applying the monthly ISR table (Article 96) and the employee's share of social security (IMSS).

steps.title: Employer Burden Summation
steps.description: Calculating employer IMSS, INFONAVIT (5%), and the specific State Payroll Tax (ISN) – usually 3%.

steps.title: Net & Total Cost Output
steps.description: Generating a breakdown of 'What the employee takes home' vs 'What it costs the company in total'.

items.title: The 25-Point Burden
items.text: On average, the 'Employer Burden' (Social Security + Taxes) adds 25% to 35% on top of the gross salary. This must be budgeted for.

items.title: UMA Value
items.text: Many social security caps are calculated based on the 'UMA' (Unit of Measure and Update), not the minimum wage. This value is updated every February.

items.title: Tax-Free Stipends
items.text: Components like 'Vales de Despensa' (Pantry Vouchers) and 'Fondo de Ahorro' can be tax-exempt for the employee if structured within legal limits.

items.title: Aguinaldo (13th Month)
items.text: A legal requirement of at least 15 days of salary, payable by December 20th. Many multinational firms offer 20-30 days to stay competitive.

items.title: Vacation Premium
items.text: Employees receive an extra 25% of their daily salary for every day of vacation taken. The base vacation starts at 12 days after year one.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Net and Gross?
faqs.answer: Gross is the salary before any deductions. Net is what hits the bank. In Mexico, the gap can be 10-30% depending on the salary bracket.

faqs.question: Is PTU included in the calculator?
faqs.answer: Profit sharing (PTU) is a variable annual payment and is usually omitted from monthly cost modeling, though it should be noted as a 10% profit-based liability.

faqs.question: Do state taxes vary much?
faqs.answer: Slightly. Most states are between 2% and 4%. CDMX and Edomex are typically at 3%.

faqs.question: What is INFONAVIT?
faqs.answer: A mandatory 5% employer-only contribution to a national housing fund for employees. It is not deducted from the employee's salary.

faqs.question: How do you calculate overtime?
faqs.answer: Calculated by hour: The first 9 hours/week are double time; anything beyond 9 hours is triple time. Our pro-calculator models these scenarios.

heroData.title: Register a Mexican Entity
heroData.subtitle: S.A. de C.V. & S. de R.L. Specialists
heroData.description: Establish your long-term presence in Mexico. We navigate the 'Secretaría de Economía' name permits, Notary Public protocols, and SAT tax registration for a seamless market entry.

steps.title: Name Authorization (SRE)
steps.description: Applying for the corporate name use permit from the Ministry of Economy. You must provide 3-5 name options in order of preference. Approval usually takes 2-5 business days.

steps.title: Drafting Articles of Association
steps.description: Defining the corporate purpose (Objeto Social), share capital, and governance structure. This must be meticulously drafted to match SAT requirements for digital invoicing capability.

steps.title: Notarization (Fe Pública)
steps.description: All founding documents must be signed before a Mexican Notary Public (Notario Público). If shareholders are abroad, apostilled Powers of Attorney (PoA) are required.

steps.title: RFC & E-Firma Acquisition
steps.description: The most critical step: Registering the company with the SAT. The Legal Representative must attend an in-person appointment to get the Tax ID (RFC) and the digital signature (e.fina).

steps.title: Foreign Investment Registry (RNIE)
steps.description: Since the entity will have foreign participation, it must be registered with the National Registry of Foreign Investments (RNIE) within 40 days of incorporation.

items.title: S.A. de C.V. (Stock Corporation)
items.text: The most popular for scalable businesses. Easier to sell shares and bring in third-party investors. Minimum of 2 shareholders required.

items.title: S. de R.L. (Limited Liability)
items.text: Similar to a US LLC. Ideal for family businesses or SMEs. More restrictive on partner entry but offers tax pass-through advantages for US parents (Check-the-box).

items.title: The Legal Representative Requirement
items.text: Every Mexican company must have a local Legal Representative (Mexican citizen or resident with an RFC). This person carries high responsibility and must often sign for bank accounts and tax filings.

items.title: Capital Requirements
items.text: While the law technically allows for 1 MXN or 2 MXN as minimum equity, we recommend at least 50,000 MXN for an S.A. to simplify initial bank account openings and visa sponsorship.

items.title: Corporate Purpose (Objeto Social)
items.text: Under the new 2021 labor laws, your corporate purpose must NOT overlap with the services you intend to outsource. It needs to be precise and descriptive.

rows.label: Notary Fees
values: Professional fees for public deed execution and register filing.

rows.label: Government Fees
values: Payment for Public Registry of Commerce (RPC) filing.

rows.label: Legal Setup (Fees)
values: Bilingual drafting, PoA management, and SAT registration assistance.

rows.label: Registered Address
values: Virtual office or physical space required for VAT-R activation.

faqs.question: Can I own 100% of the company as a foreigner?
faqs.answer: Yes. In almost all sectors (excluding specific sensitive areas like national security or oil & gas), foreign investors can own 100% of the Mexican entity.

faqs.question: Do I need to travel to Mexico to incorporate?
faqs.answer: No. You can incorporate via Power of Attorney (PoA) signed in your home country, apostilled, and sent to our team. However, opening a bank account usually requires the Legal Representative to visit in person.

faqs.question: What is the NIP?
faqs.answer: The NIP is actually called the RFC (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes). It is your 13-digit corporate tax ID used for all invoices and filings.

faqs.question: How long does it take to open a bank account?
faqs.answer: This is currently the biggest hurdle. Expect 2-4 weeks after getting the RFC. Major banks (BBVA, Banorte, Santander) have rigorous KYC/AML checks for foreign-owned entities.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, for 'VAT-R' (active tax status). The SAT often conducts physical inspections ('Verificación de Domicilio') to ensure the business is real before granting full invoicing powers.

items.title: Corporate Domicile
items.text: A physical address in Mexico is mandatory for SAT registration; virtual offices are heavily scrutinized.

items.title: Legal Representative
items.text: Must be a Mexican citizen or a resident with a valid work permit and RFC.

items.title: Shareholder PoA
items.text: Foreign shareholders must provide Apostilled Powers of Attorney to be represented at the Notary.

heroData.title: Build Your Team in Mexico
heroData.subtitle: Tech & Operational Recruitment
heroData.description: Unlock the high-potential Mexican talent market. From Guadalajara's 'Silicon Valley' tech stack to Mexico City's financial expertise, we help you source, screen, and secure the best candidates for your nearshore operations.

steps.title: Sourcing & Pipelining
steps.description: Leveraging LinkedIn, OCCMundial, and local tech communities. Focusing on candidates with high English proficiency (B2/C1) for international roles.

steps.title: Behavioral & Technical Screening
steps.description: Multi-stage interviews including cultural fit assessment and live coding challenges or technical case studies relevant to the Mexican market context.

steps.title: Background & 'Socio-Legal' Checks
steps.description: A standard practice in Mexico involving verification of RFC, CURP, and often a 'Socio-Economic Study' (investigación socioeconómica) including home visits for sensitive roles.

steps.title: Total Rewards Benchmarking
steps.description: Crafting offers that balance base salary with 'Prestaciones Superiores' (premium benefits) like GMM, pantry vouchers, and savings funds to ensure high acceptance rates.

steps.title: Offer Management & Signing
steps.description: Managing the resignation period (standard 2 weeks) and ensuring the employment contract is signed before the official start date to comply with immediate IMSS registration rules.

items.title: The Big Three Hubs
items.text: Guadalajara (IT/Electronics), Mexico City (FinTech/Services), and Monterrey (Industrial/Engineering) are the primary talent magnets. Costs and competition vary significantly between these cities.

items.title: The '13th Month' Expectation
items.text: While legal, Aguinaldo is viewed as a minimum. Offering 20-30 days of Aguinaldo is a powerful differentiator in a tight talent market.

items.title: English Proficiency Gap
items.text: While technical skills are world-class, fluid English proficiency is concentrated. You may need to pay a 15-25% premium for fully bilingual candidates.

items.title: Nearshoring Opportunity
items.text: The massive influx of US companies (Nearshoring) is driving up salaries in the northern states and CDMX. Early entry and strong employer branding are critical.

items.title: Contractor vs Employee Mindset
items.text: Most Mexican professionals prefer direct employment with full social security benefits (IMSS) over contractor status due to the long-term credit advantages (Infonavit) and healthcare.

faqs.question: What is the standard notice period in Mexico?
faqs.answer: There is no legal requirement for a notice period, but 15 days (a 'Quincena') is the professional standard. High-level executives often give 30 days.

faqs.question: Can I perform credit checks on candidates?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you require written consent. Buró de Crédito checks are common for roles in finance or those handling significant cash/inventory.

faqs.question: Are there many freelancers in Mexico?
faqs.answer: Yes, the 'Resico' (Simplified Tax Regime) has made freelancing easier. However, be careful with labor law reclassification if they work exclusively for you.

faqs.question: Which job boards are most used?
faqs.answer: OCCMundial is the market leader for local roles, while LinkedIn is dominant for tech and bilingual executive positions. Indeed is also significant for entry-level roles.

faqs.question: Is remote work জনপ্রিয় in Mexico?
faqs.answer: Extremely. Post-pandemic, tech workers in Mexico strongly prefer remote or hybrid models. The Monterrey and Guadalajara markets are highly competitive regarding remote flexibility.

items.title: The 'Hiring Manager' Interview
items.text: Personal relationships matter. Mexican candidates value meeting their direct manager early in the process to assess rapport and leadership style.

items.title: Transparency in Offers
items.text: Always clarify if the salary offered is 'Neto' (Take-home) or 'Bruto' (Gross). Candidates often talk in 'Neto' terms, while legal systems use 'Bruto'.

items.title: University Partnerships
items.text: For junior talent, partnerships with Tecnológico de Monterrey (ITESM) or UNAM are highly effective for long-term talent pipelining.

items.title: NOM-035 Mandatory Reporting
items.text: Every employer in Mexico must identify and analyze psychosocial risk factors. An HRIS that digitizes these surveys and generates the required evidence folders is a massive time-saver for potential audits.

items.title: LFPDPPP - Data Privacy
items.text: Your HRIS must comply with the Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties. This include having a clear 'Aviso de Privacidad' and 'ARCO' rights management.

items.title: Telework Expense Tracking
items.text: NOM-037 requires reimbursement of internet and electricity for remote workers. A good HRIS automates this calculation and adds it to the payroll run as a non-taxable reimbursement.

items.title: Digital Personnel Files

items.title: Vacation Law 2023 (Vacaciones Dignas)
items.text: Ensure your system is updated for the 'Vacaciones Dignas' reform, which increased the first-year minimum vacation from 6 to 12 days. Old systems often fail this tracking.

faqs.question: Does the system link to the SAT?
faqs.answer: Advanced HRIS platforms can pull the 'Constancia de Situación Fiscal' directly to verify the employee's postal code and tax regime for CFDI 4.0 compliance.

faqs.question: Can it handle biometric clock-ins?
faqs.answer: Yes, many integrate with fingerprint or facial recognition hardware. Note that under Mexican law, biometric data is considered 'Sensitive Personal Data' requiring higher security.

faqs.question: How do I handle vacation requests?
faqs.answer: The system should automatically calculate the accrual based on 'Vacaciones Dignas' rules and allow for manager approval workflows, updating the payroll system instantly.

faqs.question: Is the software available in Spanish?
faqs.answer: Crucial. For Mexican operations, the employee-facing interface must be in Spanish to ensure accessibility and avoid legal claims regarding lack of clarity in work tools.

faqs.question: Can it export to SUA/IDSE?
faqs.answer: A localized HRIS should provide CSV or text file exports formatted specifically for the IMSS's SUA and IDSE platforms to avoid manual data entry.

heroData.title: Compliant Mexican Accounting
heroData.subtitle: Electronic Accounting & NIF Standards
heroData.description: Ensure your Mexican entity is compliant with SAT's rigorous electronic accounting (Contabilidad Electrónica) requirements. We manage your general ledger, XML validation, and monthly trial balances according to Mexican Financial Reporting Standards (NIF).
heroData.bestFor: Foreign-Owned S.A. de C.V. and S. de R.L. Entities.

steps.title: CFDI Retrieval & Validation
steps.description: Downloading all issued and received XML invoices (CFDIs) directly from the SAT portal and validating their status (Active or Cancelled).

steps.title: Ledger Booking & XML Linking
steps.description: Recording transactions in the general ledger. Under Mexican rules, every accounting entry MUST be linked to the corresponding UUID of the XML invoice.

steps.title: Bank Reconciliation
steps.description: Matching bank statements with accounting records, ensuring every 'SPEI' transfer or card payment has a supporting invoice and correct VAT treatment.

steps.title: Trial Balance Generation (Balanza de Comprobación)
steps.description: Producing the monthly trial balance at a Level 2 account detail, mapped to the SAT's mandatory chart of accounts.

steps.title: Electronic Filing (Buzón Tributario)
steps.description: Uploading the XML files containing the trial balance and chart of accounts to the SAT's portal before the monthly deadline (usually the 7th or 9th of the second following month).

items.title: Contabilidad Electrónica Strictness
items.text: Missing a monthly upload of your trial balance can trigger automated fines and, more importantly, a 'Restricted' status for your digital invoicing certificate (CSD), effectively halting your business.

items.title: NIF vs IFRS/US GAAP
items.text: While Mexican NIFs are largely converged with IFRS, there are specific differences in inflationary accounting and employee benefit treatments. We provide reconciliation for corporate reporting.

items.title: The Importance of 'Polizas'
items.text: Mexican accounting is focused on the 'Póliza' (Entry Voucher). Digital accounting software must generate these pólizas with the XML UUID attached for them to be valid for tax purposes.

items.title: VAT (IVA) Creditability
items.text: An expense is only deductible and the VAT only creditable if you have the XML invoice. No XML = No deduction. This makes strict 'CFDI Control' the #1 accounting priority.

items.title: Materiality and 'Fecha de Cobro'
items.text: Mexican tax accounting is primarily 'Cash Basis' for flow-through taxes like VAT. Ensuring the 'Complemento de Pago' (Payment Receipt) is issued correctly by suppliers is critical for VAT recovery.

faqs.question: What is the Dictamen Fiscal?
faqs.answer: It is an audit report by a certified public accountant. It is mandatory only for very large companies (approx. $90M+ USD revenue) or specifically regulated entities.

faqs.question: Can I use QuickBooks or Xero in Mexico?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they are NOT sufficient for Mexican 'Contabilidad Electrónica' as they don't natively generate the required SAT XML files. You usually need a local middleware or a specialized Mexican system like Contpaqi or Aspel.

faqs.question: What happens if I lose an XML file?
faqs.answer: You can re-download it from the SAT portal (up to 5 years back). However, the invoice must have been issued to your correct RFC in the first place.

faqs.question: How long must I keep records?
faqs.answer: The statute of limitations is generally 5 years, though for certain items like capital increases or losses, records must be kept permanently.

faqs.question: Do I need a Mexican Accountant?
faqs.answer: Yes. Only a Mexican 'Contador Público Certificado' with an active SAT registration can sign off on tax filings and electronic accounting submissions.

items.title: DIOT (VAT Info Return)
items.text: Reporting of all transactions with third-party suppliers to verify VAT credits.

steps.title: Contractual Integrity Check

steps.title: Mandatory Commissions (Comisiones Mixtas)

items.title: The End of Juntas de Conciliación
items.text: Mexico is transitioning from administrative labor boards to formal Labor Courts. This shift aims for faster trials but requires even more rigorous documentation from employers.

items.title: Union Legitimacy Requirement
items.text: Under USMCA annexes, all collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) must be legitimized via secret ballot by workers. Non-compliant CBAs are considered void.

items.title: Profit Sharing (PTU) Caps
items.text: The 2021 reform capped PTU payments at the higher of 3 months' salary or the average of the last 3 years, significantly reducing risk for high-profit tech/finance firms.

items.title: Severance Liability
items.text: Unjustified termination is expensive: 3 months' salary + 20 days per year + Seniority Premium (12 days/yr). Proper performance documentation is vital to defend 'justified' cause.

items.title: REPSE Compliance Hub
items.text: If you act as a specialized service provider, you must upload your monthly IMSS/SAT/INFONAVIT evidence to the ICSOE and SISUB platforms to keep your REPSE active.

faqs.question: What is the maximum probation period?
faqs.answer: For general roles, 30 days. For management, executive, or technical roles, it can be up to 180 days. It must be in writing.

faqs.question: Is drug testing allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it is specified in the Internal Work Regulations (RIT) and the employment contract, usually for safety-sensitive roles.

faqs.question: What happens if a worker refuses to sign a termination?
faqs.answer: You must file a 'Notice of Termination' (Aviso de Rescisión) with the Labor Court within 5 days. Failure to do so makes the dismissal automatically 'unjustified'.

faqs.question: Are non-compete clauses valid in Mexico?
faqs.answer: They are controversial. While they can be signed and 'Civil' penalties agreed, the 'Right to Work' is a constitutional right, making enforcement difficult without significant financial compensation.

faqs.question: What is the mandatory training?
faqs.answer: By law, every company must have a training plan registered with the STPS to improve worker productivity and skills (Capacitación y Adiestramiento).

steps.title: VAT (IVA) Determination
steps.description: Calculating 'IVA Trasladado' (received from sales) vs 'IVA Acreditable' (paid to suppliers) on a cash basis to determine the monthly net payment or refund position.

steps.title: ISR Provisional Payment
steps.description: Calculating the monthly Income Tax (ISR) payment based on the 'Coeficiente de Utilidad' (Profit Factor) established in the previous year's annual return.

steps.title: DIP Generation
steps.description: Generating the 'Declaración de Impuestos Federales' (DIP) on the SAT portal to obtain the payment line (Línea de Captura).

steps.title: Tax Remittance
steps.description: Ensuring payment is made via the authorized Mexican bank before the 17th of the following month to avoid surcharges and late fees.

items.title: Corporate ISR Rate
items.text: Mexico has a flat corporate income tax rate of 30%. Unlike some countries, there is no progressive bracket for corporations; every dollar of taxable profit is taxed at 30%.

items.title: VAT (IVA) Standard Rate
items.text: The standard VAT rate is 16%. However, for operations in the 'Northern Border Zone', a reduced 8% rate may apply if the company meets specific registry requirements.

items.title: US-Mexico Tax Treaty
items.text: To avoid double taxation, US parents must submit form W-8BEN-E or a 'Certificate of Residence'. This can reduce withholding on technical assistance or interest payments to 5-10%.

items.title: CUFIN & CUCA Accounts
items.text: Meticulous tracking of the 'After-Tax Profit Account' (CUFIN) allows for the payment of dividends to shareholders without triggering a second layer of corporate tax.

items.title: Withholding on Dividends
items.text: Since 2014, individuals and foreign residents are subject to a 10% withholding tax on dividends paid out of Mexican profits, which may be reduced by treaties.

faqs.question: Are VAT refunds easy to get in Mexico?
faqs.answer: The SAT is generally efficient with VAT refunds for exporters ('Zero-rated' sales), but for other entities, expect a 40-70 day review process with significant documentation requests.

faqs.question: What is the statute of limitations for SAT audits?
faqs.answer: The SAT can generally audit records up to 5 years back. In cases of fraud or failure to register, this can extend to 10 years.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my car lease in Mexico?
faqs.answer: Deductibility for passenger vehicles is capped (approx. 175,000 MXN base). For electric or hybrid vehicles, the cap is much higher (250,000 MXN).

faqs.question: What is the 'Opinion of Compliance'?
faqs.answer: The 'Opinión de Cumplimiento' (32-D) is a status check (Positive/Negative) that shows if the company is up to date with filings. A positive opinion is required for all B2B contracts.

faqs.question: Do I pay tax on world-wide income?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mexican entities are taxed on their worldwide income. Foreign taxes paid can often be credited against Mexican ISR subject to limits.

items.title: Asset vs. Stock Sale Taxes
items.text: In Mexico, an 'Asset Sale' (selling machinery/contracts) triggers VAT and potential double taxation, whereas a 'Stock Sale' (selling the entity) is often more tax-efficient but carries all past tax/labor liabilities.

items.title: Labor Liability 'Contingency'
items.text: In Mexico, labor debts follow the business. If you buy a company, you inherit all severance liabilities and past social security omissions, regardless of what the SPA says.

items.title: Choice of Jurisdiction
items.text: While many MSAs use New York or Delaware law for arbitration, real estate and labor issues in Mexico MUST be governed by local law to be enforceable.

items.title: Antitrust (COFECE) Thresholds
items.text: Deals exceeding approx. $100M USD (inflation adjusted) usually require pre-approval from COFECE. Failing to file can lead to massive fines and order of divestiture.

items.title: Trusts (Fideicomisos)
items.text: Mexican Trusts are a powerful tool for deal structuring, allowing for secure 'Escrow' arrangements and complex management of collateral within the Mexican legal system.

faqs.question: Can we use 'Electronically Signed' contracts?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'E-signing' via providers like DocuSign is legal (Nom-151), but for high-value corporate transfers, a physical signature before a Notary is still required for public enforceability.

faqs.question: How long does a typical DD take in Mexico?
faqs.answer: Expect 4 to 8 weeks. Mexican companies (especially SMEs) often have decentralized records, requiring time to reconstruct corporate books and XML files.

faqs.question: Is insurance for Reps & Warranties available?
faqs.answer: It is emerging for the LATAM market. Global providers now offer policies for Mexico-centric deals, typically for transaction values over $25M USD.

faqs.question: What is the role of the Notary?
faqs.answer: Unlike in many countries, a Mexican 'Notario Público' is a senior lawyer appointed by the State. They have 'Fe Pública' (Public Faith) and their participation is mandatory for real estate and corporate changes.

faqs.question: Can foreigners be Directors?
faqs.answer: Yes. However, the 'Legal Representative' often needs to be a resident to handle SAT and local bank interactions effectively.

faqs.question: Can we manage the team directly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most Mexican firms offer 'Staff Augmentation' where you manage the daily tasks, or 'Managed Projects' where they provide the PM.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period for devs?
faqs.answer: The legal minimum is 15 days, but in the competitive tech market, 30 days is standard to ensure a smooth transition of knowledge.

faqs.question: How do you handle data security?
faqs.answer: Compliance with Mexico's Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales (LFPDPPP) is mandatory, along with standard ISO/IEC 27001 practices.

faqs.question: What are the most popular stacks in Mexico?
faqs.answer: Node.js, React, and Python dominate. However, there is a massive legacy base of Java and .NET for financial services.

faqs.question: Do I need a local entity to hire devs?

faqs.question: Can I use Spanish from Spain?
faqs.answer: Not recommended. Mexican Spanish has distinct vocabulary and tone. Using 'European Spanish' can make the brand feel distant or foreign.

faqs.question: Is Facebook still relevant in Mexico?

faqs.question: What is Profeco?
faqs.answer: The Federal Attorney's Office of the Consumer. They monitor advertising for truthfulness and can shut down campaigns that mislead consumers.

faqs.question: How do Mexicans pay online?
faqs.answer: Credit cards are growing, but 'Cash-at-OXXO' is a vital payment method for E-commerce that marketing campaigns must acknowledge.

faqs.question: Are B2B marketing tactics different?
